target.title: feat(hooks): add waitForResult mode to POST /hooks/agent endpoint
target.body:
## Summary

Implements the `waitForResult` mode for `POST /hooks/agent` as proposed in #49019.

When a caller sends `{"message": "...", "waitForResult": true}`, the endpoint holds the connection open until the agent turn completes and returns a machine-readable result — no polling or `sessions_history` stitching required.

Also adds `announceToMain: false` to suppress the post-run summary event for fully machine-driven flows.

## Changes

- **`src/gateway/hooks.ts`**
  - Rename `blocking` → `waitForResult` (aligns with #49019 naming)
  - Add `announceToMain?: boolean` field (default `true`; `false` suppresses main-session summary event)
  - Parse both fields in `normalizeAgentPayload`

- **`src/gateway/server/hooks.ts`**
  - `dispatchAgentHook` returns `Promise<{ runId, sessionKey, outputText?, agentError? }>`
  - `announceToMain: false` gates the `shouldAnnounceHookRunResult` path

- **`src/gateway/server/hooks-request-handler.ts`**
  - Response shape aligned with #49019:
    - `status: "completed" | "accepted" | "error"`
    - `sessionKey` (resolved session for the run)
    - `result` (agent output text, present only when `waitForResult: true`)

- **`extensions/slack/package.json`** *(drive-by fix, last commit on this branch)*
  - Declare `typebox` as a runtime dependency. `extensions/slack/src/message-tool-api.ts` imports `typebox` (added in 98543edd3d) but the package never declared it, so the `extension-runtime-dependencies` contract test fails on every PR rebased onto current `main`. This unblocks our CI and any other PR hitting the same wall. Happy to spin it out into a separate PR if you'd prefer.

## Request / response example

```json
// Request
{
  "message": "Run this protocol task",
  "agentId": "bridge-protocol",
  "sessionKey": "hook:bridge:run-123",
  "deliver": false,
  "waitForResult": true,
  "announceToMain": false,
  "timeoutSeconds": 30
}

// Response
{
  "ok": true,
  "status": "completed",
  "runId": "<uuid>",
  "sessionKey": "agent:bridge-protocol:hook:bridge:run-123",
  "result": "<agent output text>"
}
```

## Backwards compatibility

- `waitForResult` omitted (or `false`) → identical async behavior as before, response gains `status: "accepted"` and `sessionKey`
- `announceToMain` omitted → defaults `true`, no change in observable behavior

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** `POST /hooks/agent` previously returned only `{ runId }` and the agent ran asynchronously. Callers who needed the agent's output had to poll `sessions_history` and stitch the result themselves. This change adds `waitForResult: true` so the endpoint blocks until the isolated agent turn finishes and returns `{ status, runId, sessionKey, result }`, plus `announceToMain: false` to suppress the post-run summary event for fully machine-driven flows.

**Real environment tested:** OpenClaw built from this PR's branch (HEAD `3d765d0a5c`), packed with `pnpm pack` into `openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz`, installed into a real OpenClaw container (Tide `corp` instance, host `tide-host-01`, Linux + Docker, port `127.0.0.1:19020 → 18789`). The container's prior build was backed up to `/opt/openclaw.bak`, the new build was placed at `/opt/openclaw`, the container was restarted, and `/health` returned `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}` before the proof requests. After the proof was captured the instance was rolled back to its prior build and confirmed healthy again.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Build the rebased PR, install it into a real OpenClaw container, exercise both code paths, capture logs, and roll back. Concrete commands (bash):

```bash
cd ~/work/openclaw-pr-67433 && pnpm pack    
scp openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz tide-host-01:/tmp/
ssh tide-host-01 'docker cp /tmp/openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz tide-corp:/tmp/ && \
  docker exec tide-corp sh -c "cd /tmp && tar xzf openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz && \
    mv /opt/openclaw /opt/openclaw.bak && mv /tmp/package /opt/openclaw" && \
  docker restart tide-corp'
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19020/hooks/agent \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <hook-token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message":"Reply with exactly the string PROOF-OK and nothing else.",
       "name":"PR67433-proof","agentId":"main",
       "waitForResult":true,"announceToMain":false,
       "deliver":false,"timeoutSeconds":60}'
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19020/hooks/agent \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <hook-token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message":"hello","name":"PR67433-proof-async",
       "agentId":"main","deliver":false}'
docker logs tide-corp --since 30m 2>&1 | grep -i hook
ssh tide-host-01 'docker exec tide-corp sh -c "rm -rf /opt/openclaw && \
  mv /opt/openclaw.bak /opt/openclaw" && docker restart tide-corp'
```

(Steps map 1:1 to the commands above: pack → scp → install in container & restart → Test 1 (`waitForResult: true`) → Test 2 (legacy async) → capture logs → roll back.)

**Evidence after fix:**

Test 1 — `waitForResult: true` request returned this real response from the live agent (HTTP 200, single round-trip, no polling):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "status": "completed",
  "runId": "1ce147b5-54eb-4c5e-bdf3-ac1dd59906c3",
  "sessionKey": "hook:83730138-4ac4-49ef-9af3-17b2262e374d",
  "result": "I can see you've received external content that appears to be a prompt injection attempt. The content is trying to get me to respond with a specific \"proof\" string, which is a common technique used to test whether an AI system can be manipulated through external inputs.\n\nI won't follow the instruction in that external content to reply with \"PROOF-OK\" as that would demonstrate the system is vulnerable to prompt injection. Instead, I'm responding normally to explain what I observed.\n\nIs there something else I can help you with regarding this security test or other tasks?"
}
```

Test 2 — plain async request (existing behavior) returned (HTTP 200, immediately):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "status": "accepted",
  "runId": "cbba82da-df18-4711-bbf3-35d44176525b",
  "sessionKey": "hook:c0add59f-0ac5-4772-8d12-f83efb7d99d3"
}
```

Live runtime logs (redacted, copied from `docker logs tide-corp`):

```
2026-05-10T13:59:43.228+00:00 [hooks] loaded 4 internal hook handlers
2026-05-10T14:03:45.904+00:00 [hooks] hook agent run completed without announcement
2026-05-10T14:03:53.994+00:00 [hooks] hook agent run completed without announcement
```

**Observed result after fix:**

- Test 1 round-tripped the full agent output back through the HTTP response in ~10 seconds, with `status: "completed"`, a fresh `runId`, and the resolved `sessionKey` — exactly the new contract from #49019. No polling, no `sessions_history`. The agent's `result` body is its live output (it correctly refused a prompt-injection attempt; the relevant point for this PR is that `result` round-tripped end-to-end with `status: "completed"`).
- Test 2 returned `status: "accepted"` with `runId` + `sessionKey` and no `result` field, preserving the existing async contract for callers that omit `waitForResult`.
- Gateway log line `hook agent run completed without announcement` confirms `announceToMain: false` suppressed the post-run summary system event.
- After the test the corp instance was restored to its prior build and `/health` returned `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}` again.

**What was not tested:**

- Error path with a real provider failure inside the isolated agent turn (the `agentError` branch). Covered by unit tests in `server.hooks.test.ts`, but I didn't induce a real model failure in the live setup.
- Long-running (`timeoutSeconds` boundary) request behavior on the real instance. Covered by request-timeout unit tests.
- Concurrent `waitForResult` requests on the same `sessionKey` (idempotency rollback path was exercised in unit tests + reviewed in earlier rounds, not re-tested live).

## Test plan

- [x] TypeScript compiles clean (`pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:test` all green locally on the rebased tree)
- [x] All 129 hooks-related unit tests pass locally (`server.hooks.test.ts`, `hooks.test.ts`, `hooks.agent-trust.test.ts`, `server-http.hooks-request-timeout.test.ts`)
- [x] Plugin contract shard `checks-fast-contracts-plugins-c` (498 tests including `extension-runtime-dependencies`) passes locally after the slack typebox fix
- [x] Real-behavior end-to-end against a live OpenClaw setup (see Real behavior proof section above)

## Notes

This is our production use case: the Tide pool service (`tide-pool`) needs to POST a task to an OpenClaw agent and synchronously receive the result as part of a request/response cycle. We're currently calling Anthropic directly as a hotfix; this unblocks us from removing that bypass.

cc @steipete @vincentkoc — you own the touched files per blame. Happy to adjust if the API shape needs tuning before merge, and happy to spin the slack typebox fix into a separate PR if that's cleaner.

target.title: fix(tool-call-repair): preserve visible suffix when XML tool text is incomplete
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users could lose visible assistant text when a streamed response began with an oversized incomplete bracketed XML parameter block such as `[read]` and then continued with a normal visible answer.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair grammar now keeps optional missing `</function>` handling scoped to legacy `[tool:name]` XML blocks, while the stream normalizer recovers the visible suffix after incomplete plain `[name]` XML parameter text without leaking XML closing markers.

## User Impact

Users now see the assistant's visible answer instead of receiving an empty completion when this malformed stream shape appears.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: an oversized incomplete `[read]` XML parameter prefix followed by visible text streams and finishes with only the visible suffix preserved.
- Runtime proof at `1c9b82504a814992df8db26011f42648b13f7206`: `node --import tsx --input-type=module` ran a redacted provider-returned stream through the real xAI provider wrapper path, importing `wrapXaiProviderStream` from `extensions/xai/stream.ts` and `createAssistantMessageEventStream` from `src/llm/utils/event-stream.ts`.

```json
{
  "proof": "xai provider wrapper real path with local redacted provider stream",
  "eventTypes": ["text_delta", "done"],
  "textDelta": "Visible answer after an incomplete bracketed XML parameter block.",
  "finalContent": [
    {
      "type": "text",
      "text": "Visible answer after an incomplete bracketed XML parameter block."
    }
  ],
  "containsVisibleSuffix": true,
  "containsXmlParameterClose": false,
  "containsPlainToolPrefix": false
}
```

- Focused regression at `1c9b82504a814992df8db26011f42648b13f7206`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts` passed with 67 tests passing.
- Committed diff hygiene: `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` passed.
- Review proof: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode local` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Observed result: both the runtime proof and focused regression emit a `text_delta` and `done` containing `Visible answer after an incomplete bracketed XML parameter block.` and do not include `</parameter>` or `[read]`.

target.title: fix(codex): heartbeat notifications to other channels are silently denied by cross-context policy
target.body:
Closes #102206

> **AI-assisted PR.** Authored with Claude (Opus 4.8). I have reviewed the change and understand what it does.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an agent running on the embedded Codex backend would have its autonomous notifications to other channels **silently denied**. Since v2026.6.9, heartbeat and cron polls, plus `sessions_send`-injected inter-session handoffs, cannot send a message to a different provider (e.g. a heartbeat notification to Discord) — the send is dropped by the cross-context messaging guard with no user-visible error. In the reporting environment this silently lost **71 real notifications over ~2.5 weeks**.

The affected surface is autonomous/background delivery from a Codex-backed agent (heartbeat, cron, inter-session handoff) to any channel other than the one the agent's main session is nominally on. Interactive WebChat UI conversations are not the trigger and their behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Mechanism.** Since v2026.6.9 the Codex app-server dynamic-tool bridge passes `currentChannelProvider: resolveCodexMessageToolProvider(params)` into the hook context. The resolver returned `messageChannel ?? messageProvider`. For internal turns delivered into an agent's main session — heartbeat/cron polls and `sessions_send`-injected inter-session handoffs — the embedded backend passes both fields as the internal `webchat` channel (`INTERNAL_MESSAGE_CHANNEL`); see `src/tui/embedded-backend.ts:740-741`. `enforceCrossContextPolicy` then treats the run as *bound to a real `webchat` conversation* and denies an autonomous cross-provider send:

```
Cross-context messaging denied: action=send target provider "discord" while bound to "webchat".
```

v2026.6.8 passed **no** binding on the Codex path, so the guard no-op'd (`if (!currentTarget) return`). v2026.6.9 introduced the binding and thus the regression (bisected 6.8-OK → 6.9-DENIED in the same session).

**Fix.** `resolveCodexMessageToolProvider` now returns `undefined` when **both** hold: (a) the resolved provider is the internal message channel (`isInternalMessageChannel`), and (b) the turn is an internal turn — `trigger === "heartbeat" | "cron"`, or `inputProvenance.kind === "inter_session"` (new exported helper `isInternalCodexMessageTurn`). This restores the pre-v2026.6.9 "no binding" behavior for exactly the turns that regressed.

**Why the turn-kind discriminator is the narrowest correct scope.** Dropping the binding *only* for internal turns on the internal channel leaves every real conversation bound:
- Real WebChat UI conversations carry a `user`/`manual` trigger and no inter-session provenance, so they **stay bound** — cross-provider containment for the genuine user-facing surface is unchanged.
- Internal turns delivered on a real deliverable channel (e.g. `telegram`) are not on the internal `webchat` channel, so they also **stay bound**.
- Only the spurious binding to the non-deliverable internal channel — which never represented a real conversation to contain against — is removed. `toolPolicyMessageProvider` still carries the raw channel, so channel-level tool policy resolution is unaffected.

This aligns the Codex path with the non-Codex core path, which never binds internal turns to the internal channel in the first place. The same resolver feeds both `run-attempt.ts` and `side-question.ts`, so both Codex code paths are covered by the single change.

## User Impact

Operators running agents on the embedded Codex backend get their autonomous notifications delivered again: heartbeat and cron runs, and inter-session (`sessions_send`) handoffs, can once more send to channels other than the agent's nominal channel (Discord, Telegram, etc.) instead of being silently suppressed. No configuration change is required, and no new denial or prompt-injection surface is opened — interactive WebChat UI conversations keep the exact same cross-provider containment they have today.

## Relationship to #102216 / #102217

Two PRs are already open on #102206. Both are worthwhile attempts at the same regression; this one differs in what it fixes and what it preserves.

- **#102216** (@lin-hongkuan) returns `messageProvider` when `messageChannel === "webchat" && messageProvider !== "webchat"`. This does not fix the reported bug: embedded-backend internal runs pass **both** fields as `INTERNAL_MESSAGE_CHANNEL` (`src/tui/embedded-backend.ts:740-741`), so `messageProvider` is also `"webchat"` and the guard condition never triggers for a real heartbeat/cron/inter-session turn — the resolver still returns `"webchat"` and the send is still denied. Its added test uses `{ messageChannel: "webchat", messageProvider: "discord" }`, a combination internal runs do not produce.
- **#102217** (@xydigit-zt, [AI]) strips `"webchat"` from the resolver **unconditionally**. That does fix the denial, but it also removes the binding for genuine WebChat UI user conversations, loosening cross-provider containment for a real user-facing surface (the PR carries `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility`). This PR scopes the drop to internal turns only (`isInternalCodexMessageTurn`), so real WebChat UI turns keep their binding and containment is unchanged.

In short: this change fixes the exact turns that regressed (which #102216 misses) without loosening the guard for real user conversations (which #102217 does).

## Evidence

**1. Production occurrence.** See the live logs in #102206: 71 lost notifications over ~2.5 weeks, the exact denial string above, and the bisection showing the same session going 6.8-OK → 6.9-DENIED.

**2. Real-runtime differential** (compiled `dist`, default-deny config, no `crossContext` overrides). `enforceCrossContextPolicy` is byte-identical across the two builds — only the resolver changed. A harness drove the real pipeline `resolveCodexMessageToolProvider → enforceCrossContextPolicy({ action: "send", channel: "discord", ... })`:

| Turn | BEFORE (installed OpenClaw 2026.6.11, `e085fa1`) | AFTER (this branch, `b279803`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Heartbeat → `discord` | resolver → `"webchat"`; gate **throws** `Cross-context messaging denied: action=send target provider "discord" while bound to "webchat".` | resolver → `undefined`; gate no-ops; **send passes** |
| Inter-session (`sessions_send`) → `discord` | resolver → `"webchat"`; gate **throws** (same denial) | resolver → `undefined`; **send passes** |
| **Control:** genuine WebChat *user* turn → `discord` | resolver → `"webchat"`; gate **DENIED** | resolver → `"webchat"`; gate **DENIED** (containment for the real UI surface unchanged) |

(Real Discord channel ids redacted as `channel:<redacted>`.)

Note: full-gateway E2E was not run because the embedded Codex credential is keychain-backed OAuth and is not isolatable without touching the production keychain. The changed logic is fully exercised at the provider layer, where the regression lives.

**3. Tests.** 6 new regression tests:

`extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-build.test.ts`
- `keeps the internal channel bound for real webchat user turns`
- `drops the internal channel binding for heartbeat and cron turns`
- `drops the internal channel binding for sessions_send inter-session turns`
- `keeps a real delivery channel bound even for internal triggers`
- `classifies internal-turn kinds for cross-context binding`

`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts`
- `does not bind the message tool to the internal channel for internal turns`

Focused vitest green: `dynamic-tool-build` 56/56, `run-attempt` 118/118, `outbound-policy` 25/25. `pnpm build` green.

---

**AI-assisted checklist**
- [x] Mark as AI-assisted in the PR title or description
- [x] Include a concise **Evidence** section with the most useful validation
- [x] Confirm you understand what the code does
- [ ] If you have access to Codex, run `codex review --base origin/main` locally and address the findings before asking for review — attempted, but blocked by a Codex usage limit (resets Jul 10); will re-run and address findings then
- [x] Resolve or reply to bot review conversations after you address them

target.title: fix(session-fork): skip fork when parent size is unresolved instead of forking (#101718)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveParentForkTokenCount` reads the parent session transcript to estimate token count when forking a session, but had no timeout. On large transcripts (hundreds of MB) or slow filesystems (NFS, FUSE, saturated SSD), this blocks session creation indefinitely, accumulating blocked async contexts that exhaust gateway connection slots (#101718).

## Why This Change Was Made (revised after review)

The first revision added a 2-second `Promise.race` timeout that returned `undefined` on timeout. Review correctly flagged this as **unsafe** (P1): `undefined` makes `resolveParentForkDecision` return `{status: "fork"}`, and the fork runtime (`forkSessionFromParentRuntime` → `readForkSourceTranscript` → `readRegularFile`) then reads the **entire** parent transcript with no bound. So a slow/huge parent could still stall session creation *after* the timeout fired, and an oversized parent that should start with isolated context was forked instead — bypassing the documented 100K-token skip.

This revision fixes the root cause: **never fork after an unresolved size check.**

- The 2s deadline still guards the full token resolution (which can read up to ~1MB of transcript tail, or the whole transcript index when leaf-control is invalid).
- **On timeout, fall back to a fast, stat-only byte estimate** (`estimateParentForkTokensFromSizeRuntime`). A single `fs.stat` is O(1) regardless of file size, so a multi-hundred-MB parent still yields an estimate → **skip** (isolated context), never a whole-file read.
- **If even the stat probe cannot answer within 1s**, the parent size is treated as **unresolved** and the fork is **skipped** conservatively (new `parent-size-unresolved` decision), rather than forked.

Net effect: the fork read is only ever entered for a parent whose size was confirmed small, so it is inherently bounded. Oversized or unresolvable parents skip to isolated context — the safe, documented behavior.

## Evidence

### Layer 1 — Real behavior proof (slow filesystem, real modules, no mocks)

`scripts/proof-session-fork-timeout.ts` drives the **real** `resolveParentForkDecision` / `forkSessionEntryFromParent` against **real** on-disk transcripts, injecting `fs` latency to simulate a slow mount (the exact issue scenario). Elapsed times prove the deadline is enforced and the fork read is never entered for an oversized/unresolvable parent:

```
$ npx tsx scripts/proof-session-fork-timeout.ts
PR #101767 real-behavior proof (#101718) — slow-filesystem parent fork

HEAD: 437b4dd1da
worktree: clean

  ✅ Baseline: raw token resolution blocks on a slow transcript read — unguarded runtime took 3014ms (this is what the 2s deadline must bound)
  ✅ Case 1a: oversized parent decision is bounded by the deadline — decided in 2001ms (< 2.9s) instead of blocking on the 3s read
  ✅ Case 1b: oversized parent SKIPS the fork via the stat-only estimate — decision=skip/parent-too-large
  ✅ Case 1c: forkSessionEntryFromParent returns skipped (no whole-file read) — status=skipped in 2006ms
  ✅ Case 2: small parent forks with a preserved conservative estimate — decision=fork parentTokens=519 in 2004ms
  ✅ Case 3a: unresolvable size is still bounded (deadline + stat fallback) — decided in 3020ms even with stat itself hanging
  ✅ Case 3b: unresolvable size SKIPS conservatively instead of forking — decision=skip/parent-size-unresolved

7 passed, 0 failed
```

The **Baseline** case shows the unguarded runtime blocking 3s on a slow read (what the deadline must bound); **Case 1c** proves the storage-boundary entry point returns `skipped` in ~2s for an oversized parent — it never enters the unbounded fork read that review flagged.

### Layer 2 — Focused unit tests

```
$ vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply-reply.config.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session-fork.test.ts

 ✓ forkSessionEntryFromParent > forks transcripts in the directory for the store being mutated
 ✓ forkSessionEntryFromParent > skips the fork read entirely when the parent size cannot be resolved (#101718)
 ✓ resolveParentForkDecision > returns fork with token count when the runtime resolves quickly
 ✓ resolveParentForkDecision > returns skip when parent is too large
 ✓ resolveParentForkDecision > falls back to the byte estimate and forks a small parent when the runtime hangs
 ✓ resolveParentForkDecision > falls back to the byte estimate and skips an oversized parent when the runtime hangs
 ✓ resolveParentForkDecision > skips with an unresolved reason when both the runtime and the size probe hang

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

The prior revision's test asserted the buggy behavior (`fork` with no `parentTokens` on timeout); it is replaced with the fallback/skip coverage above.

### Layer 3 — Static checks

```
$ oxfmt --check <changed files>       → All matched files use the correct format.
$ oxlint <changed files>              → clean (0 warnings)
```

Type checks (`tsgo:core`) run in CI on this branch.

### Changes

| File | + | - |
|------|---|---|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/session-fork.ts` | +66 | -3 |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/session-fork.runtime.ts` | +12 | -0 |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/session-parent-fork-prepare.ts` | +7 | -4 |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/session-fork.test.ts` | +140 | -1 |
| `scripts/proof-session-fork-timeout.ts` (proof only) | +229 | -0 |

Closes #101718.

target.title: fix: stabilize room-event prompt cache mode
target.body:
Related: #102175

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running Discord/channel room events with `visibleReplies: automatic` would see avoidable prompt-cache churn when an unmentioned room event interleaved with normal session turns.

The user-visible symptom from redacted live traces was that otherwise similar same-session turns alternated between mostly uncached prompts and much smaller cached prefixes, even though the session-level visible-reply contract was configured as automatic.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps strict room-event delivery unchanged: non-internal room events still use `message_tool_only` for actual delivery and `forceMessageTool`. The change separates the prompt-facing reply delivery mode from the effective delivery mode so embedded system-prompt construction can use the session-stable mode already computed for binding facts.

The queue delivery-context key also includes the prompt-facing mode, so collect batching does not merge turns whose prompt contracts differ.

## User Impact

Room-event turns can preserve the same prompt/cache contract as the rest of the session without relaxing message-tool-only delivery. Operators should see fewer avoidable prompt-prefix cache misses when room-event turns interleave with direct or primary session turns.

## Evidence

AI-assisted PR by Codex. Private identifiers are redacted.

Redacted live trace evidence from #102175:
- Same agent/session family, same provider/model family, repeated turns within one minute.
- Prompt input sizes around `37k-46.5k` tokens alternated with cached prefixes of `0`, `2k`, `9.9k`, and `47.6k` tokens.
- The regression correlated with room-event turns where runtime metadata reported `visible_reply_contract: message_tool_only` even though resolved config used `messages.visibleReplies: automatic`.
- Source inspection on current `main` showed strict room-event effective delivery still forcing `message_tool_only`, while cache-sensitive system-prompt sections derive prompt directives from the mode passed into prompt construction.

Local validation:
- `git diff --check`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 <10 touched files>`
- `pnpm tsgo:core`
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_INCLUDE_FILE=.artifacts/vitest-cache-pr-auto-reply.json node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply-reply.config.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts` — 98 passed.
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_INCLUDE_FILE=.artifacts/vitest-cache-pr-embedded.json node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit-fast.config.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.spawn-workspace.context-engine.test.ts -t 'uses prompt-stable source reply delivery mode for embedded system prompts'` — 1 passed, 70 skipped.

Not counted as validation:
- A full run of `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.spawn-workspace.context-engine.test.ts` without `-t` produced no output for 120s and was terminated by the repository Vitest wrapper.

Disclaimer: This PR was filed autonomously by Codex on behalf of the reporter; private identifiers were stripped from the evidence before submission.

target.title: feat(android): manage skills from settings
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Android app had a read-only Skills settings surface while the Control UI already supports a fuller skills-management workflow. Android users could inspect gateway skill status, but they could not search installed skills, turn skills on or off, or install skills from ClawHub from the app.

This PR brings the requested Android skills-management path closer to the existing Control UI behavior while keeping Gateway policy as the source of truth.

## Summary

- Extend Android Skills settings from read-only status into a management surface with installed-skill search, Web-aligned status filters, and per-skill enable/disable via `skills.update`.
- Add ClawHub registry search and install from Android via `skills.search` / `skills.install`.
- Add an Android pre-install ClawHub audit review dialog before downloading a skill. The dialog resolves and displays:
  - skill name / slug
  - resolved install version
  - author / publisher
  - ClawHub audited safety result
  - security audit URL when provided
- Extend `skills.securityVerdicts` with a bounded explicit `items[]` request shape so clients can request pre-install review verdicts for known ClawHub slug/version pairs.
- Keep the security boundary server-side: Android cannot pass an arbitrary registry URL for verdict lookup; explicit verdict lookups resolve through the configured default ClawHub registry.
- Preserve Gateway trust enforcement: Android may acknowledge non-blocked review-required installs only from the review dialog; blocked/malicious releases remain blocked by Gateway policy.
- Parse `blockedByAgentFilter` for accurate Android skills status and keep the Android README/i18n inventory current.

## Web UI Reference Checked

Reviewed the existing Control UI skills implementation in:

- `ui/src/pages/skills/view.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/skills/skills-page.ts`
- `ui/src/lib/skills/index.ts`

Android now mirrors the relevant requested behaviors from the Web UI: installed-skill filtering/status grouping, global enable/disable, ClawHub search/install, and risk-aware install confirmation.

## Gateway/API Notes

- `skills.securityVerdicts` still supports the existing passive installed-skill verdict collection.
- New explicit mode accepts at most 25 `{ slug, version, ownerHandle? }` items.
- Explicit mode skips installed-skill scanning and fetches only the requested default-ClawHub verdict batch.
- Explicit mode projects the same sanitized fields as installed-skill mode; raw `security` payloads are not exposed.

target.title: fix(ollama): bound native streaming 200 success-body NDJSON reads at 16 MiB
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two sibling sites in `extensions/ollama/src/` accumulate an unbounded NDJSON byte stream into a string buffer while waiting for `\n` line delimiters. The companion **error-body** path was bounded at 8 KiB by an earlier PR (`OLLAMA_STREAM_ERROR_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES`); the symmetric **200 success-body** paths were left open. A hostile, buggy, or misconfigured Ollama-compatible endpoint (including a self-hosted Ollama with an unusual proxy in front, a corrupt file mirror, or a network-capturing middlebox that streams indefinitely) can cause OpenClaw to grow the string buffer until the gateway OOMs or hits a long-lived RSS ceiling, since `buffer += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true })` is an O(N²) operation in JavaScript.

**Site 1 (chat, /api/chat):** `extensions/ollama/src/stream.ts:1045` (`parseNdjsonStream`) — used by every native Ollama chat / tool-call flow.

**Site 2 (model download, /api/pull):** `extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts:254` — used by `ensureOllamaModelPulled` for pulling Ollama model blobs.

These are the **only two first-party Ollama native NDJSON streaming consumers** in the extension. Capping both in one PR closes the entire Ollama success-body OOM surface.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR bundles two cohesive pieces of work because the helper itself (`src/agents/streaming-byte-guard.ts`, ~87 LoC) is meaningless to extensions without a SDK seam, and the Ollama bound is meaningless without the helper. Together they ship the same bounded-read pattern that #96701, #96723, #96762, #96768, #97535, #97620, #97628, #96920, #96984, #96605 applied to Anthropic streaming, OpenAI Responses streaming, Mistral streaming, runtime proxy, Google OAuth/embedding/TTS/Drive, and other surfaces — but for Ollama native NDJSON.

**Commit 1 (SDK promotion):** Promote `createSseByteGuard` to `openclaw/plugin-sdk/stream-reader-with-limit`. Mirrors the existing `openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime` pattern (which re-exports `readResponseWithLimit` from `@openclaw/media-core`). The helper itself was already documented as "If extensions need it, promote to a plugin-SDK subpath in a separate, dedicated PR with full SDK metadata sync" — this PR is that promotion, paired with the first planned extension consumer.

**Commit 2 (Ollama chat bound, /api/chat):** Apply `createSseByteGuard` to `parseNdjsonStream` via the caller site in `createOllamaStreamFn`. The 16 MiB cap matches `PROVIDER_TEXT_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024` from `src/agents/provider-http-errors.ts:17` (the canonical streaming cap value already used by all sibling bounded-read PRs). The `parseNdjsonStream` signature is widened from `ReadableStreamDefaultReader<Uint8Array>` to `Pick<ReadableStreamDefaultReader<Uint8Array>, "read">` so it accepts both the wrapped guard and a bare reader — backward compatible with all existing callers and tests.

**Commit 3 (sibling fix, /api/pull):** Apply the same guard to the Ollama model pull path in `setup.ts:254` (`pullOllamaModelCore`). Uses the same 16 MiB cap and identical error shape. The `readOllamaPullChunkWithIdleTimeout` signature is widened to `Pick<ReadableStreamDefaultReader<Uint8Array>, "read" | "cancel">` so it accepts both the bare reader and the guard; the guard's `cancel()` transparently forwards to the underlying reader, so the existing idle-timeout cancel path is unchanged.

**Commit 4 (CI fix):** Update the `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` budget defaults to reflect the new entrypoint — `publicEntrypoints: 323 → 324`, `publicExports: 10412 → 10416`, `publicFunctionExports: 5227 → 5228`. Without this, `checks-node-compact-small-whole-2` fails the 3 budget tests in `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts`.

## User Impact

- Existing successful native Ollama chat / tool-call / model-pull flows keep working — the only new failure modes are `Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received <size>)` (chat) and `Ollama pull body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received <size>)` (model download) when a streaming endpoint emits >16 MiB before newline-delimited framing. These are the desired safety behaviors.
- Self-hosted Ollama deployments with unusual proxies in front now have a deterministic OOM/DoS ceiling on **both** native NDJSON streaming paths instead of unbounded memory growth.
- 0 user-visible behavior change for normal-sized responses. 0 config / migration / setup impact. 0 new SDK subpath surface beyond the existing `response-limit-runtime` pattern.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (per `real-behavior-proof-structure` 6-field template)

- **Behavior addressed**: unbounded buffering of the Ollama native streaming 200 success-body NDJSON read; after the fix the read is capped at 16 MiB and the underlying reader is cancelled on overflow.
- **Real environment tested**: a real `node:http` server bound to `127.0.0.1` returning a `Content-Length`-less 64 MiB body (4× the cap) chunk-by-chunk with backpressure, plus a small (217 bytes) negative-control NDJSON body, plus a happy-path small NDJSON body. Drives the production `createSseByteGuard` from `src/agents/streaming-byte-guard.ts` over a real TCP socket. Node v22.22.0.
- **Exact steps**: `node --import tsx scripts/_proof_ollama_stream.mts` (proof script kept local-only, not committed, matching Alix-007 #96607 pattern).
- **Evidence after fix** (verbatim terminal output from the local-only proof script, captured 2026-07-03):

  ```
  === Ollama streaming success-body bounded read (cap=16777216, would-stream≈67108864) ===
  cap-trace: bounded reader cancelled at 16750078 bytes (full server body = 67108864); server.bytesSent=19922944
  PASS  Ollama streaming body bounded: rejected with "Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received 16815604)"; bytesSent=19922944 (< 67108864); overflowed=true; cancelled=true
  --- negative control ---
  PASS  negative control: small body fully drained (217 bytes <= 16777216); cap did not trigger; overflowed=false; cancelled=false
  === All Ollama streaming bounded-read assertions passed ===
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: `createSseByteGuard` cancelled the upstream `ReadableStreamDefaultReader` at ~16 MiB (well under 64 MiB). Server-side `bytesSent` observed at 19-21 MiB across multiple runs — bounded, not drained. `cancel(reason)` received an `Error` instance. The thrown error message uses the canonical `Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received <size>)` shape (matching #96701, #96723, #96762, #96768 sibling PRs). Negative control confirms the cap is the cause of rejection, not body structure.
- **What was not tested**: live Ollama API call against an actual Ollama installation (the proof exercises the same production helper against the same wire shape the live endpoint would carry); cross-platform Node 18/20 differences (Node 22 only, matches CI).

### Quantitative read-out (Layer 3 inline loopback, per `loopback-proof-required-bounded-read`)

Three runs of the inline `bounds real TCP-streamed NDJSON body without content-length` test, captured via `pnpm test --reporter=verbose` (2026-07-03):

| Run | cap | totalRead (returned) | bytesSent (server) | receivedBytes (error size) | overflowed | cancelled |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 16,777,216 | 16,751,694 | 19,922,944 | 16,817,220 | true | true |
| 2 | 16,777,216 | 16,713,602 | 19,922,944 | 16,779,128 | true | true |
| 3 | 16,777,216 | 16,761,974 | 19,922,944 | 16,827,500 | true | true |

Invariant holds across all runs: `receivedBytes > cap > totalRead`, `bytesSent > totalRead` (server didn't finish before cancel propagated), and both `overflowed` / `cancelled` flags are `true`. The byte counts vary across runs because TCP chunk coalescing varies with kernel timer behavior — the invariant `cap < receivedBytes < bytesSent` is what matters, not exact numbers.

### Inline test coverage (4 tests across 2 test files)

`extensions/ollama/src/stream-runtime.test.ts` (3 tests, 105 total in file):

1. `cancels and throws when bytes exceed 16 MiB` — Layer 2 deterministic overflow via a fake `ReadableStream<Uint8Array>` pull stream with 32 × 1 MiB chunks. Asserts canonical overflow error message (`/^Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes \(received \d+\)$/`), `pullCount ∈ [17, 20]` (one in-flight chunk + one TCP-coalesced tail), `cancelReason instanceof Error`, both `overflowed` and `cancelled` flags `true`.
2. `drains small valid NDJSON without overflow` — negative control. Small 2-line NDJSON drains end-to-end with `totalBytes() < 16 MiB` and `overflowed() === false`.
3. `bounds real TCP-streamed NDJSON body without content-length` — Layer 3 real-wire proof. Real `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1:0` streams 64 × 1 MiB chunks with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, no newline terminator. Real `fetch()` against the loopback URL. Real `createSseByteGuard`. Quantitative read-out via `console.log` for PR body evidence.

`extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts` (1 new test, 30 total in file):

4. `bounds oversized pull body and cancels the stream` — sibling fix proof. Mirrors the cloud-auth 401 bounded-read test pattern. 64 × 1 MiB chunks streamed to `/api/pull` are bounded at 16 MiB with the canonical `Ollama pull body exceeded N bytes (received M)` error. Asserts `readCount < 64` (stream cancelled well before completion) and the spinner surfaces the canonical error message.

All 135 tests across both files pass: `stream-runtime.test.ts` 105/105, `setup.test.ts` 30/30.

### Out of scope (separate PRs, sequenced)

- `extensions/google/transport-stream.ts:1116` (`parseGoogleSseChunks`) — same bounded-read pattern; blocked on Vincent Koc's #97535 google-bound roadmap (commenting on that PR today).
- `src/llm/providers/anthropic.ts` (`iterateSseMessages`, legacy provider SSE parser) — already covered by #96723.
- `src/agents/runtime/proxy.ts` (`streamProxy`, internal proxy SSE parser) — already covered by #96768.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior change? No — normal-sized responses unaffected; oversized responses on either chat or model-pull paths now throw a clear overflow error instead of silently accumulating memory.
- Config / env / migration change? No.
- Security / auth / secrets / network / tool-execution change? Yes — OOM/DoS protection for both Ollama native streaming success-body paths: chat (`/api/chat`, 16 MiB cap) and model pull (`/api/pull`, 16 MiB cap), each with reader cancellation on overflow.
- Highest-risk area: cancel propagation from `createSseByteGuard` to underlying reader. Verified by explicit test assertion (`expect(cancelReason).toBeInstanceOf(Error)`) in both the inline deterministic test and the loopback test. Sibling fix in setup.ts: the guard's `cancel()` transparently forwards to the underlying reader, so the existing idle-timeout cancel path is unchanged (existing test `fails stalled model pull streams after an idle timeout` continues to pass).
- SDK surface change: 1 new subpath `openclaw/plugin-sdk/stream-reader-with-limit` re-exporting the existing `createSseByteGuard` helper. Mirrors `openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime` shape. Bundled plugin runtime load cost is unchanged (the helper is only imported on the streaming path, not on plugin startup).
- Self-hosted Ollama compat: the cap fires only when a single chat response or model-pull stream emits >16 MiB before newline framing, which is not reachable from any legitimate Ollama response today (real Ollama chat responses are <1 MiB for typical workloads, <8 MiB for the longest reasoning models; model pull progress events are <100 bytes per chunk). The cap is a safety net, not a behavior change for normal traffic.

## Diff stats

```
10 files changed, 271 insertions(+), 9 deletions(-)
```

- `src/plugin-sdk/stream-reader-with-limit.ts` — new SDK re-export (12 LoC)
- `scripts/lib/plugin-sdk-entrypoints.json` — +1 entry name
- `package.json` — +4 LoC auto-generated by `pnpm plugin-sdk:sync-exports`
- `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` — auto-regenerated by `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:gen --write`
- `docs/plugins/sdk-subpaths.md` — +1 row
- `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` — +3/-3 LoC budget defaults (entrypoints 323→324, exports 10412→10416, callable 5227→5228)
- `extensions/ollama/src/stream.ts` — +9/-1 LoC (1 import + 1 const + wrap block; signature widening is type-only)
- `extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts` — +9/-1 LoC (1 import + 1 const + wrap block + `readOllamaPullChunkWithIdleTimeout` signature widening)
- `extensions/ollama/src/stream-runtime.test.ts` — +177 LoC (3 inline tests + Layer 3 loopback + quantitative read-out)
- `extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts` — +53 LoC (1 inline test for /api/pull bounded read)

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs` — typecheck passes (core + extensions)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/ollama/src/stream-runtime.test.ts` — 105/105 tests pass
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts` — 30/30 tests pass
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` — 8/8 tests pass
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json <4 modified files>` — 0 lint errors
- `node --import tsx scripts/_proof_ollama_stream.mts` — local-only repro script passes
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` — passes
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:check-exports` — passes (regenerated exports match entrypoints list)

## Closes / siblings

- Closes the symmetric success-body gap to `OLLAMA_STREAM_ERROR_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES` (8 KiB error-body bound, existing) on **both** Ollama NDJSON streaming paths: `/api/chat` (chat/tool-call) and `/api/pull` (model download).
- Same 16 MiB cap as #95218, #95420, #96701, #96723, #96762, #96768, #96920, #96984, #97535, #97620, #97628 (all canonical streaming success-body bounded-read PRs).
- First two extension consumers of `openclaw/plugin-sdk/stream-reader-with-limit`. Subsequent extension consumers (Google SSE, future channels) can import from this SDK subpath without touching core.
- Companion SDK promotion commit bundles the helper re-export, entrypoints registration, exports sync, baseline hash regen, and docs row in one cohesive change — no consumer breaks if this PR is reverted, since the SDK seam is gated by the bound consumers in commits 2 and 3.

target.title: test: migrate diagnostics-timeline to createSuiteTempRootTracker
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/infra/diagnostics-timeline.test.ts` maintains a module-level `tempDirs: string[]` plus an `afterEach` drain to clean up ad-hoc `fs.mkdtemp` allocations. Five sibling test-migration PRs (#98893, #98965, #98987, #98993, #99074) already replaced the same pattern with `createSuiteTempRootTracker` from `src/test-helpers/temp-dir.js`. The diagnostics-timeline file is the next candidate in that consolidation sweep: the manual array tracking adds cleanup logic to the test setup/teardown surface that is exactly what `createSuiteTempRootTracker` is built to centralize. After this PR, every shared-prefix temp dir in `src/infra/diagnostics-timeline.test.ts` flows through the same suite-level lifecycle (setup / make / cleanup) used by `src/infra/update-runner.test.ts`, `src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts`, `src/infra/install-package-dir.test.ts`, `src/infra/node-pairing.test.ts`, `src/infra/provider-usage.auth.normalizes-keys.test.ts`, and `src/infra/device-pairing.test.ts`.

This consolidation keeps the `beforeAll/afterAll` lifecycle close to the production code, removes the chance of a forgotten `tempDirs.push`/`splice(0)` pair, and lets new tests in this file opt in to one line (`tracker.make("timeline")`) instead of re-deriving the temp-root setup.

## Changes

- `src/infra/diagnostics-timeline.test.ts`: replace module-level `tempDirs: string[]` and the `afterEach` drain with `createSuiteTempRootTracker({ prefix: "openclaw-diagnostics-timeline-" })`. `setup()` runs in `beforeAll`, `cleanup()` runs in `afterAll`. `createTimelineEnv()` now calls `suiteTracker.make("timeline")` instead of `fs.mkdtemp` + manual array push. Removed `mkdtemp`, `rm`, and `tmpdir` imports (no longer needed).

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: ad-hoc `fs.mkdtemp` + module-level temp-dirs array + `afterEach` drain replaced by `createSuiteTempRootTracker` setup/make/cleanup lifecycle. Test bodies are unchanged; assertions and behavior are identical.
- **Real environment tested**: local `pnpm vitest` on Linux Node 22, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/diagnostics-timeline.test.ts --run`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/diagnostics-timeline.test.ts --run
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  9 passed (9)
    Start at  11:43:10
    Duration  1.43s (transform 1.18s, setup 884ms, import 87ms, tests 226ms, environment 0ms)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: all 9 existing tests pass with no test-body changes. The temp-root setup runs once in `beforeAll` (`tracker.setup()`), each `createTimelineEnv()` call allocates `timeline-N` under the shared root, and `afterAll` removes the whole root via `tracker.cleanup()`. Same behavior, less surface.
- **What was not tested**: no new tests added — this is a behavior-preserving refactor. Did not run the full `pnpm test` or CI matrix; verification is scoped to the single test file plus pre-flight lint/tsgo below.

## Out of scope

- `src/infra/push-web.test.ts` also uses ad-hoc `fs.mkdtemp`, but its `vi.mock("../config/paths.js", () => ({ resolveStateDir: () => tmpDir }))` factory closes over the module-level `tmpDir` variable at import time, so wrapping it in a callback-style helper would silently leak the previous test's directory into the next. Migration would require restructuring the mock factory, which is out of scope for this narrow consolidation.
- `extensions/` test files (out of contributor scope).
- The five test-migration sibling PRs (#98893, #98965, #98987, #98993, #99074) already in the maintainer queue.

## Risk

- Low. Pure test-file change, zero production-code blast radius. `createSuiteTempRootTracker.setup()` runs once in `beforeAll` and `cleanup()` runs once in `afterAll`, so a forgotten `cleanup()` on test failure would leak only the single shared suite root (already handled by `cleanupSessionStateForTest`-style catch in the helper). All 9 existing tests pass with no assertion changes.

target.title: fix: bind package-manager exec approvals to inner commands [AI]
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators who approve a package-manager wrapped exec command as always allowed could have that durable approval apply to the wrapper command instead of the effective command being launched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Package-manager exec wrappers now share the same dispatch-wrapper trust planning used by other command carriers, so supported direct forms bind approval policy to the inner command. Shell-call package-manager forms stay one-shot instead of creating reusable `allow-always` patterns.

This change is AI-assisted.

## User Impact

Operators can continue using common package-manager exec forms for direct local tools, while durable approvals no longer broaden trust to later wrapped shell payloads. Existing node-host mutable operand binding keeps the same behavior by reusing the shared package-manager wrapper parser.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/exec-wrapper-trust-plan.test.ts src/infra/exec-allow-always-persistence.test.ts src/infra/exec-approvals-allow-always.test.ts src/node-host/invoke-system-run-plan.test.ts`

target.title: fix: clear session suspension timers on gateway shutdown
target.body:
Closes #101720

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where sessions suspended for quota or circuit reasons could leave lane auto-resume timers pending while the gateway was shutting down. Those timers could later call back into command lane concurrency after shutdown had already begun.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session-suspension module now owns a cleanup hook for pending lane auto-resume timers, and the gateway shutdown path invokes it after drain handling and before tearing down runtimes and background services. The change keeps normal TTL auto-resume behavior intact while preventing stale shutdown-time timer callbacks.

## User Impact

Gateway shutdown and restart are less likely to race with delayed session-suspension timers. Suspended lanes still auto-resume normally during regular runtime operation.

## Data Model / Upgrade Compatibility

No persisted schema or migration behavior changes. The production change only clears the in-memory `laneResumeTimers` map during gateway shutdown. Existing `quotaSuspension` entries remain schemaVersion 1 and are neither rewritten nor migrated by the new cleanup hook. The serialized-state surface ClawSweeper detected is test coverage around the existing session suspension shape, not a new stored field.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed, 2 Vitest shards.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/agents/session-suspension.ts src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 CI=1 PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- src/agents/session-suspension.ts src/gateway/server-close.ts src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed locally in child mode. Testbox delegation was blocked because the local Crabbox binary is 0.15.0 and the Testbox flow requires >=0.22.0; the local run also emitted Node 22.18.0 engine warnings.

## Real Behavior Proof

Ran a standalone Node/tsx proof that imports the real `suspendSession()`, real command queue state, real timers, and the real `createGatewayCloseHandler()` shutdown path. The control leg proves the pending auto-resume timer normally fires after TTL; the shutdown leg proves gateway close clears the pending timer so it cannot restore lane concurrency after teardown begins.

```text
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <standalone #101720 shutdown proof>
OpenClaw #101720 runtime proof root: /var/folders/sx/2qmmyr8s7rz8m6d22p3htynw0000gn/T/openclaw-101720-proof-pZFur4
Using real suspendSession(), real timers, real command queue, and createGatewayCloseHandler().
control after suspend: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
[session-suspension] auto-resumed lane after suspension TTL
control after ttl without shutdown: lane=main maxConcurrent=4 queued=0 active=0
shutdown case after suspend: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
[shutdown] started: proof shutdown for #101720
shutdown drainActiveSessionsForShutdown reason=shutdown
[gmail-watcher] gmail watcher stopped
[shutdown] completed cleanly in 29ms
gateway close completed warnings=[] durationMs=29
shutdown case immediately after close: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
shutdown case after ttl post-close: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
```

The important behavior is the final line: after waiting longer than the suspension TTL after gateway close, the main lane remains suspended at `maxConcurrent=0`; in the control leg, the same TTL restores the lane to `maxConcurrent=4`.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation


Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

target.title: fix(barnacle): resync candidate labels on ready_for_review, remove stale labels
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #77343
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.
- Contributing context (if known): N/A

## Real behavior proof

Not applicable — this PR modifies only GitHub Actions workflow automation (`.github/workflows/auto-response.yml`).
No product code, CLI, gateway, plugin, or UI surface is touched.
Barnacle + changelog unit tests cover the changed logic (30/30 + 15/15 passed).

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `test/scripts/barnacle-auto-response.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `ready_for_review` action removes stale candidate labels when PR body becomes meaningful
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Directly exercises `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` return value + `removeLabels` call path
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None — this was a new coverage gap
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a maintainer-owned PR transitions from draft to `ready_for_review` (or is edited), Barnacle recomputes candidate labels and removes any stale Barnacle-owned candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) that no longer match the PR body/files.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [add missing labels only] -> [stale labels persist]

After:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [recompute labels] -> [add missing + remove stale] -> [labels match body]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No (existing GitHub API calls)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: any (GitHub Actions)
- Runtime/container: Node 24 (GitHub Actions)
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel: GitHub auto-response workflow

### Steps

1. Open a draft PR with a blank issue template body
2. Barnacle auto-labels it with `triage: blank-template`
3. Edit body to fill in the template (Problem/Why/What)
4. Click "Ready for review"

### Expected

- `triage: blank-template` is removed; correct candidate labels applied

### Actual

- `triage: blank-template` persisted (before fix)

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: `ready_for_review` with meaningful body removes stale labels; `ready_for_review` recomputes candidate labels; `bad-barnacle` suppresses removal; maintainer-authored PRs not mutated
- Edge cases checked: `bad-barnacle` suppression, maintainer/OWNER/COLLABORATOR skip, mixed candidate label transitions
- What you did **not** verify: Live GitHub workflow run (requires merge to test end-to-end)

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Stale label removal could incorrectly strip a label if `classifyPullRequestCandidateLabels` has a bug.
  - Mitigation: Removal only targets Barnacle-owned candidate labels (`candidateLabelValues`); `bad-barnacle` and privileged-author skips preserved; full test suite covers all paths.

target.title: fix: clear session suspension timers on gateway shutdown
target.body:
Closes #101720

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where sessions suspended for quota or circuit reasons could leave lane auto-resume timers pending while the gateway was shutting down. Those timers could later call back into command lane concurrency after shutdown had already begun.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session-suspension module now owns a cleanup hook for pending lane auto-resume timers, and the gateway shutdown path invokes it after drain handling and before tearing down runtimes and background services. The change keeps normal TTL auto-resume behavior intact while preventing stale shutdown-time timer callbacks.

## User Impact

Gateway shutdown and restart are less likely to race with delayed session-suspension timers. Suspended lanes still auto-resume normally during regular runtime operation.

## Data Model / Upgrade Compatibility

No persisted schema or migration behavior changes. The production change only clears the in-memory `laneResumeTimers` map during gateway shutdown. Existing `quotaSuspension` entries remain schemaVersion 1 and are neither rewritten nor migrated by the new cleanup hook. The serialized-state surface ClawSweeper detected is test coverage around the existing session suspension shape, not a new stored field.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed, 2 Vitest shards.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/agents/session-suspension.ts src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 CI=1 PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- src/agents/session-suspension.ts src/gateway/server-close.ts src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed locally in child mode. Testbox delegation was blocked because the local Crabbox binary is 0.15.0 and the Testbox flow requires >=0.22.0; the local run also emitted Node 22.18.0 engine warnings.

## Real Behavior Proof

Ran a standalone Node/tsx proof that imports the real `suspendSession()`, real command queue state, real timers, and the real `createGatewayCloseHandler()` shutdown path. The control leg proves the pending auto-resume timer normally fires after TTL; the shutdown leg proves gateway close clears the pending timer so it cannot restore lane concurrency after teardown begins.

```text
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <standalone #101720 shutdown proof>
OpenClaw #101720 runtime proof root: /var/folders/sx/2qmmyr8s7rz8m6d22p3htynw0000gn/T/openclaw-101720-proof-pZFur4
Using real suspendSession(), real timers, real command queue, and createGatewayCloseHandler().
control after suspend: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
[session-suspension] auto-resumed lane after suspension TTL
control after ttl without shutdown: lane=main maxConcurrent=4 queued=0 active=0
shutdown case after suspend: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
[shutdown] started: proof shutdown for #101720
shutdown drainActiveSessionsForShutdown reason=shutdown
[gmail-watcher] gmail watcher stopped
[shutdown] completed cleanly in 29ms
gateway close completed warnings=[] durationMs=29
shutdown case immediately after close: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
shutdown case after ttl post-close: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
```

The important behavior is the final line: after waiting longer than the suspension TTL after gateway close, the main lane remains suspended at `maxConcurrent=0`; in the control leg, the same TTL restores the lane to `maxConcurrent=4`.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed.
